subject.title: refactor: own model discovery by runtime lifecycle

question: Should the released Plugin SDK permanently expose the new prepared-catalog readers while retaining `loadModelCatalog` as a deprecated compatibility facade, and what deprecation commitment should OpenClaw make to external plugins?
rationale: The implementation can preserve source compatibility mechanically, but only maintainers can choose the durable external SDK boundary and its removal policy.

options.title: Approve the staged SDK transition
options.body: Keep `loadModelCatalog` deprecated, document `loadPreparedModelCatalog` and `getPreparedModelCatalogSnapshot` as the supported replacements, and merge the lifecycle refactor.

options.title: Keep the legacy SDK surface unchanged
options.body: Avoid publishing new prepared-catalog calls until maintainers define a narrower public Plugin SDK contract, retaining the internal lifecycle work behind existing APIs.

options.title: Pause for SDK design review
options.body: Defer this branch until the owner of the Plugin SDK specifies the compatibility window and intended replacement API shape.

recommendation.title: Approve the staged SDK transition
recommendation.body: Keep `loadModelCatalog` deprecated, document `loadPreparedModelCatalog` and `getPreparedModelCatalogSnapshot` as the supported replacements, and merge the lifecycle refactor.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor owns the current implementation and its stated compatibility facade, making them the best available person to turn the selected SDK direction into a bounded merge-ready patch.
